content:
ashley: Heads up, I'm seeing a short-lived latency spike (~120-180ms) for text-gen requests during autoscale increases in us-west-2 around 23:12 UTC.
priya: Which pool? dedicated or ephemeral?
ashley: This is the private cluster warm-handshake path — new replicas joining the warm pool. Not the usual warmpool starvation we saw last month.
ryan: Any KV cache change or quantization rollout?
ashley: No rollout. KV miss rate jumped from 4% -> 28% on those joining workers in the 30s window.
liz: Can you paste the trace id / sample req?
ashley: trace=trc_03a1d. Sample tail: 
```
latency: 150ms
step: provisioner.assign -> 40ms
step: kernel_probe -> 60ms
step: kv_prefetch -> 30ms
step: runtime-accept -> 20ms
```
priya: kernel_probe taking 60ms is suspicious. We usually see <10ms.
ryan: profiler output from the joining pod?
ashley: grabbing perf stat now, but quick top shows a short CPU spin in runtime_main while kernel selection heuristics probe multiple kernels.
ashley: perf snippet:
```
# runtimesctl profile --pod joiner-7 --last 2m
samples: 184
80% runtime_main::select_kernel
10% allocator::cuda_init
5% kv::prefetch
5% other
```
liz: select_kernel doing lots of JIT-ish checks? Could be probing quantized vs fp kernels sequentially, causing retries.
priya: Also saw a pattern where when many joiners start at once, they contend for the kernel cache lock and that magnifies latency. Could be a lock convoy.
ryan: Does the provisioner batch start signals? If it fires multiple join tasks in parallel we may get N joiners trying same kernel lookups.
ashley: Provisioner is configured to handshake concurrently for up to 8 pods. Today we had spikes of 12 simult joins due to a scale step.
priya: Ok hypothesis: elevated concurrency -> kernel-selection probe sequence -> kernel-cache lock contention -> KV prefetch delayed -> higher end-to-end latency.
liz: Quick mitigations: reduce concurrent handshake limit to 4 on the provisioner, and add backoff/randomized jitter to kernel probe path.
ryan: Can we push a quick canary change to set handshake_limit=4 on the scale-controller config in staging and monitor?
ashley: Doing it now. Patching controller config via k8s patch: `kubectl -n infra patch cm scale-controller --patch '{"data":{"handshake_limit":"4"}}'`
deploy-bot: deploy start: scale-controller config patch to infra/scale-controller cm (user=ashley)
priya: Also add a metric for kernel-probe-lock-wait-ms so we can alert if >25ms for >1% of joins.
ryan: I'll add the metric and a grafana panel.
ashley: After handshake_limit change, I see join latency drop to ~30-40ms in the same load window. KV miss bounce still small but not correlated.
priya: Great. Next steps: (1) instrument probe lock durations, (2) introduce jitter/backoff in probe sequence, (3) consider optimistic lockless cache read with fallback.
liz: I'll open an infra RFC for the kernel probe flow and include microbenchmarks for 1/4/8 concurrent joiners.
ashley: Filing incident doc with traces + perf dumps. Follow-up: schedule a short retro with runtime and provisioner owners.
sre-metrics-bot: metric alert created: kernel_probe_lock_wait_ms P95 > 25ms -> notify eng-runtime@pagerduty
priya: Thanks everyone.
ryan: label: mitigated (handshake_limit lowered). Monitor for 1h then revert to previous if stable.
ashley: Agree. I'll keep posting updates here. :thumbsup:"
